record.original_question: What is the local deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical G2-manifolds? More specifically, can one understand the local geometry of their moduli space, prove a uniqueness result for the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, decide whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries, and determine the properties of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons, including whether that projection is surjective?

evidence.quote: An obvious problem in this context is to understand the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds; i.e. the deformation theory of such G2-instantons. This is currently being investigated by Joe Driscoll (a PhD student of Derek Harland) and would potentially help solve several interesting questions. For example, can one prove a uniqueness result for the 'basic' G2-instanton on R^7 [GN95] (which has gauge group G2)? Do deformations of G2-instantons with symmetries on AC G2-manifolds also have symmetries? A positive answer to the latter question would mean that we could describe (at least a component) of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds with a cohomogeneity-1 action via the techniques and results described in this survey. There will also be a natural projection map in this context from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons (studied in [CH16]), and so it would be interesting to understand the properties of this map, e.g. whether it is surjective.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^7, \varphi, g)$ be an asymptotically conical $G_2$-manifold; that is, a complete 7-manifold equipped with a torsion-free $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ (with associated metric $g$) which, outside a compact set, is asymptotic at a polynomial rate to the Riemannian cone $C(\Sigma) = (\mathbb{R}_{>0} \times \Sigma, dr^2 + r^2 g_\Sigma)$ over a nearly Kähler 6-manifold $(\Sigma, g_\Sigma)$. Let $P \to M$ be a principal $G$-bundle with compact structure group $G$. A $G_2$-instanton on $P$ is a connection $A$ whose curvature $F_A$ satisfies $F_A \wedge \psi = 0$, where $\psi = *\varphi$. Asymptotic to a fixed dilation-invariant $G_2$-instanton on $C(\Sigma)$ (equivalently, a pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills/$SU(3)$-instanton on $\Sigma$), one obtains a moduli space $\mathcal{M}(M)$ of asymptotically conical $G_2$-instantons on $M$ and a moduli space $\mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$ of nearly Kähler instantons on $\Sigma$, together with a natural restriction-to-link projection $\pi:\mathcal{M}(M) \to \mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$.

Address the following:

(a) Describe the local structure of $\mathcal{M}(M)$ near a given asymptotically conical $G_2$-instanton (its expected dimension, obstruction theory, and smoothness conditions).

(b) Prove a uniqueness statement for the "basic" $G_2$-instanton on $\mathbb{R}^7$ with gauge group $G_2$ (the canonical $G_2$-instanton built from the spin connection / octonionic structure on flat $\mathbb{R}^7$): show that, within an appropriate class of asymptotically conical $G_2$-instantons on $\mathbb{R}^7$ with gauge group $G_2$, the basic instanton is the unique solution.

(c) Suppose $H$ is a Lie group acting on $(M, \varphi)$ by $G_2$-automorphisms preserving a given $H$-invariant $G_2$-instanton $A_0$. Show, or determine the obstructions to showing, that every sufficiently small deformation of $A_0$ within $\mathcal{M}(M)$ is gauge-equivalent to an $H$-invariant connection.

(d) Determine geometric and analytic properties of the projection $\pi:\mathcal{M}(M) \to \mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$; in particular, decide whether $\pi$ is surjective.
artifact.status_search_result: Joe Driscoll's 2020 PhD thesis (University of Leeds) "Deformations of Asymptotically Conical G2-Instantons" develops the local deformation theory addressing part (a), relating deformations to the kernel of a twisted Dirac operator on M and to eigenvalues on the nearly Kähler link. Subsequent work (e.g., Driscoll's paper on G2-instantons on the spinor bundle of S^3, J. Geom. Anal. 2024) builds on this. The full uniqueness of the basic G2-instanton on R^7, the symmetry-preservation question for general H, and surjectivity of the projection to the nearly Kähler instanton moduli space do not appear settled in the literature, so the overall problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.snippet: PhD thesis developing deformation theory of asymptotically conical G2-instantons via twisted Dirac operators on M and on the nearly Kähler link.

status_evidence.title: G2-Instantons on the Spinor Bundle of the 3-Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs and studies G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds, building on the deformation framework.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work uses the AC deformation framework but does not resolve all listed sub-questions.

status_evidence.title: Deformation theory of asymptotically conical Spin(7)-instantons
status_evidence.snippet: Analogous AC deformation theory developed in the Spin(7) setting, citing the G2 case.
status_evidence.claim: Parallel deformation theory exists; G2 case provides foundation but open sub-problems remain.
